title: Nem tud + Infinitive: Explaining Why You Can't

sections.title: Negating tud, then giving a reason
sections.content: To say you're not able to do something, just negate the conjugated tud, exactly like any other verb — Nem tudok, nem tudsz, nem tud, and so on, still followed by the infinitive. You already know mert ("because") from earlier units, so you can now explain the reason for the missing skill in the same breath.

sections.title: nem tud + infinitive + mert...
rows: Nem tudok úszni, mert sosem tanultam.
I can't swim, because I never learned.
Petra nem tud vezetni, mert nincs jogosítványa.
Petra can't drive, because she doesn't have a license.
Nem tudunk énekelni, mert nincs tehetségünk hozzá.
We can't sing, because we have no talent for it.

items.spanish: Tamás nem tud jól főzni, mert soha nem gyakorolt.
items.english: Tamás can't cook well, because he never practiced.
You can't play the piano? Why not?

sections.content: Every reason here points back to the person: never learned, no license, no talent, never practiced. That's the signature of nem tud — the missing piece is something about YOU. Keep that in mind for the next grammar point, where the missing piece is about the SITUATION instead.
